description.narrative:
The proposed TEA program will contribute to the following outcomes:
UNSDCF Outcome 3: Palestinian governance institutions, processes, and mechanisms at all levels are more democratic, rights-based, inclusive, and accountable
UNDP/PAPP PPF Outcome 1: Improved democratic governance based on the principles of human rights and rule of law, with equitable access to justice and quality public and basic services
Indicative Output(s) with gender marker:
Output 1: Improved capacities of government institutions for effective and efficient management of public resources in an inclusive and accountable manner
Output 2: Improved capacities of public and private service providers for more accountable, inclusive, effective and efficient service provision

The TEA program aims at improving The government performance and responsiveness to Palestinian citizens. It will target areas critical to public trust in the government by producing and using robust evidence and analysis to facilitate stakeholder engagement and advocacy between the government and citizens, whilst providing technical assistance to the relevant authorities to enable it to respond effectively

description.narrative:
The information below is based on annual reports, annual meetings, field-visits and correspondence with the UNDP.
As the previous year, the context was was one marked by hardship, primarily due to the war in Gaza and the deteriorating situation in the West Bank, and a resulting financial crisis. On the other hand, the UNDP assesses that the new (19th) government, which was inaugurated in April 2024, is motivated to engage with citizens, civil society, and the private sector to move the reform agenda forward.
During the period, some key achievements can be highlighted.
Government institutions adopted programme-supported digital systems and transparency mechanisms. By the end of 2025, 118 public institutions had adopted programme-supported solutions, including digital citizen budgets, digital licensing and accreditation systems, property tax services, municipal e-services and public service centres. The report also states that 49 government institutions were applying improved transparency practices through measures such as publication of digital citizen budgets, digitalisation of services and application of sectoral corruption risk management.
These digital solutions include digital Citizen Budgets for 22 ministries, enabling public access to budget information; digital property tax services within the Ministry of Finance; a digital Licensing and Accreditation system in the Ministry of Health; a National Registry for Persons with Disabilities as well as public service centres and e-service portals at local-government level.
The digitalization of additional tax services led, according to UNDP:s estimate, to an additional 119 000 USD in tax revenue collection.
In the health sector, TEA3 has continued to institutionalize Patient Care Evaluation Systems (PCES) across hospitals and health directorates and Local Hospital Boards (LHBs) in all government hospitals. A particularly notable result was that Local Hospital Boards mobilized approximately USD 2.4 million in financial and in-kind contributions during 2025, supporting hospital improvements, equipment acquisition, and service upgrades. Hospital management became more participatory and accountable. Community leaders, medical professionals, and local stakeholders became actively involved in oversight and resource mobilization, leading to measurable improvements in healthcare infrastructure and services.
The programme contributed to changes in the way Palestinian public institutions and civil society organisations work by introducing and institutionalising new systems, coordination mechanisms and digital services.
The Palestinian Anti-Corruption Commission (PACC), together with the Ministries of Finance and Health, completed sectoral corruption risk assessments and prepared for institutionalisation of the Sectoral Corruption Risk Management methodology across additional government sectors. According to the report, this has strengthened the capacity of PACC and participating ministries to identify and manage corruption risks using a structured methodology.
Support to the Palestinian NGOs Network contributed to renewed coordination among Palestinian civil society organisations. Six thematic sector groups were reactivated, stakeholder mapping was completed and efforts continued to strengthen the Civil Society Coordination Council. According to the report, this has improved coordination between sectoral working groups and laid the foundation for more structured engagement between civil society and government.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
